# dzsum1

> Forms the 1-norm of the complex vector using the true absolute value.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dzsum1 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dzsum1';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dzsum1( N, x, strideX ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of elements in the vector CX. |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | CX |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | StrideCX |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of elements in the vector `CX`.
- `x`: The vector whose elements will be summed.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: sum of absolute values

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dzsum1.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX ) → number
```

Takes the sum of the absolute values of a complex vector and returns a.
double precision result.

Based on DZASUM from Level 1 BLAS. The change is to use the 'genuine'
absolute value (cabs) rather than dcabs1.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Complex input vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride for `CX` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `CX` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of elements in the vector `CX`.
- `x`: The vector whose elements will be summed.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: sum of absolute values

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

## Notes

-   `dzsum1()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DZSUM1`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dzsum1.f).

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import dzsum1 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dzsum1';

// Sum of the moduli |x| over all elements:
const x = new Complex128Array( [ 3.0, 4.0, -6.0, 8.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dzsum1( 3, x, 1 );
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 16.0

// Using the ndarray interface (last two elements only):
out = dzsum1.ndarray( 2, x, 1, 1 );
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 11.0
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DZSUM1`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DZSUM1 takes the sum of the absolute values of a complex vector and returns a double precision result.

Based on DZASUM from the Level 1 BLAS. The change is to use the 'genuine' absolute value.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
